text.p: Greek construction firm Hellenic Technodomiki said its 96 pretax profit rose 12.2 percent to 2.75 billion drachmas from 2.45 billion in 1995, its shareholder relations officer told Reuters.
Turnover also rose 15 percent to 24.5 billion drachmas from 21.3 billion in 1995.
The company intends to raise its 1996 dividend per share to 180 drachmas from 170 a year earlier.

"Our company has acquired construction firm Kastor, which will enable it to participate in projects worth up to 2.5 billion drachmas," said Stergios Pitoskas. Kastor has a Z-class construction licence.
Before the acquisition of Kastor, Technodomiki was not able to participate in similar projects, he added.
Technodomiki also acquired property development firm Peira whose sole asset is real estate, Pitoskas added.
Technodomiki was cooperating with another Greek construction company Avax in a $38 million project in Moldavia for the construction of an oil terminal on the Danube river, he said.
The two companies had the same level of participation in the concession for the project whereas Technodomiki had undertaken the oil terminal's construction, he added.
The project is primarily financed by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.

Technodomiki is currently involved in the Rio-Antirio bridge and Elefsis-Stavros highway projects and is also participating in the buy-out of Cambas Wineries along with other Greek construction companies, he said.
Its order book of uncompleted projects stood at 75 billion drachmas, he said.
Shares of Hellenic Technodomiki closed down 100 drachmas at 3,900.
